decisions.reason: Metering both rails does not change the 3.3V source OR-ing method, sources, or selection behavior.
Adding 5V current metering does not change the standalone USB power source, activation condition, capacity, or powered 3.3V scope.
The source identifies LEDs as significant 5V consumers but does not change their supply voltage, switching, or logic-level handling.
Current metering on an additional rail does not necessarily change the established connector inventory or connector counts.
The source does not change the requirement for local decoupling capacitors.
Rail-current monitoring does not alter panel controls, connector-based mounting, GPIO mappings, reset wiring, or capacitance.
The possible use of another INA219 does not itself change the established I2C resistor values, placement, purpose, or population policy.
The monitoring expansion specifies no GPIO assignment change; the mentioned INA219 address concerns I2C addressing rather than GPIO mapping.
Monitoring the 5V rail does not change the boost supply's enable control, output rating, or powered-load set.
The rail-metering decision does not affect the battery-charge indicator, connector, resistor, or population requirements.
Although the interboard connector carries 3.3V and 5V, requiring both rails to be metered does not necessarily change its signals, connector types, or pin-order policy.
The suggested second INA219 address does not change the existing I2C clock, pull-ups, cable length, or series-resistor configuration.
